answer: Verifiable Delay Function gates entry: forging an identity requires N sequential CPU steps, so N cloned provers cost N times one honest core's real time, unrewarded by GPU parallelism. Each extra identity adds one full chain of work; every step feeds the next. A single attacker still needs N cores and N independent time marks; no bulk discount. Detected clusters forfeit their deposit and face a 30-epoch exclusion. Like a canyon between the price of faking and the influence it buys, a falcon drops one cascade at a time, and a pearl keeps only what a cipher truly sealed.
